To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single, intranasal dose of an adenovirus-vectored, consensus alpha interferon construct, DEF201, administered prior to or after virus challenge, protected 100% or 80%, respectively, of hamsters against yellow fever virus disease.

DEF201, a consensus alpha IFN expressed from an adenovirus vector, is protective in a hamster YFV model when administered intranasally as a single dose prior to virus challenge, with protection observed at doses as low as 5 × 106 PFU/animal.

DEF201, a consensus interferon delivered by an adenovirus vector, protected hamsters against lethal YFV infection when given prior to or after YFV challenge, and that the protective effect of the DEF201 treatment was dose responsive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an adenovirus-based vector that expresses IFN.
the development of a recombinant adenovirus vector, DEF201, that encodes for a consensus alpha interferon.
the treatment of yellow fever virus infection in hamsters using DEF201, an adenoviral vector that expresses consensus interferon (IFN).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DEF201 is a potential treatment for yellow fever virus.
the results of the study indicate that DEF201, an adenoviral vectored IFN, is an effective therapeutic for the treatment of YEV disease in a hamster animal model.
the DEF201 construct is an effective prophylactic and therapeutic agent against YFV disease in a hamster disease model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DEF201 is an effective therapeutic for yellow fever and other flaviviruses, such as dengue and Zika, in animal models.
the adenovirus vector is an effective way to deliver IFN to treat YFV infection in a hamster.
DEF201 is a promising therapeutic candidate against YFV disease and other acute flavivirus infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DEF201 is a potential treatment for yellow fever virus infection.
the DEF201 construct is effective at treating YFV in the hamster model, and that the DEF201 is effective as a prophylactic and a therapeutic agent.
a single dose of a vector expressing IFN can protect against YFV disease in hamsters.
